title: Renter Friendly Upgrades That Won't Cost Your Deposit
h1: Renter Friendly Upgrades: Removable Ways to Make Your Apartment Look High-End
description: The best renter friendly upgrades for lighting, walls, kitchens and baths, with costs, difficulty and how to reverse each one before your move-out day.
secondary_keywords: how to decorate a rental without damaging walls
excerpt: Lighting, hardware, removable wallpaper and smarter ways to hang art: renter friendly upgrades rated by cost, difficulty and how easily you can undo them.
image_alt: Framed art hung above a console in a rental apartment, an example of renter friendly upgrades that avoid wall damage
key_takeaways: Check your lease and get written landlord approval before painting, drilling or swapping fixtures.
Keep every original part in labeled bags and photograph the apartment before you start.
Bulbs, lamps, curtains, rugs and cabinet hardware deliver the biggest change for the least risk.
Test peel-and-stick products on a hidden spot first; they can lift paint, especially on flat finishes.
Leaning art and picture ledges let you decorate walls with few or no holes.

faq.q: What upgrades can renters do without landlord permission?
faq.a: It depends on your lease, but changes that involve no alteration at all are generally safe: bulbs, lamps, rugs, freestanding furniture, tension rods, leaning art and textiles. Anything involving paint, drilling, adhesives, wiring or plumbing may be restricted, so read your lease and ask your landlord in writing before starting.

faq.q: How do you decorate a rental without damaging walls?
faq.a: Lean large art and mirrors on ledges, consoles or the floor, use tension rods for curtains in window recesses, and use adhesive strips only for light frames within their weight rating. If your lease allows small nail holes, picture hooks with thin nails are often cleaner than adhesives, and the holes are easy to fill with spackle.

It can. Peel-and-stick wallpaper usually removes cleanly from well-cured satin or eggshell paint, but it may lift flat or freshly applied paint, and it gets harder to remove over time. Test a sample on a hidden spot for a week, apply to clean walls, and peel slowly at a low angle when removing.

faq.q: Can I change the light fixtures in my apartment?
faq.a: Often yes, with landlord approval. Keep the original fixture and all its hardware, turn off the breaker before working, and hire a licensed electrician if you are not confident with wiring. Reinstall the original fixture before you move out unless your landlord agrees in writing to keep the new one.

faq.q: What renter friendly upgrades add the most value?
faq.a: Warm, high-CRI bulbs, extra lamps or plug-in sconces, floor-length curtains hung high, a properly sized area rug and new cabinet hardware give the biggest visual change for the cost. All of them are inexpensive, easy to reverse, and most can come with you to your next apartment.
